recommendations.action: Replace the informal 'top 50% by value_score' retention targeting rule with the budget-constrained ILP optimizer.
recommendations.why: At equal budget and RM capacity, the optimizer protects 64% more net expected value than the current heuristic -- same spend, better targeting.
recommendations.confidence: High -- this is a mechanical improvement (better use of already-validated effect sizes and existing constraints), not a new causal claim.
recommendations.next_step: Pilot the optimizer's account list against the heuristic's list on one month's retention run; compare realized churn, not just the modeled projection.

recommendations.action: Formalize the 30%-withdrawal -> RM-outreach trigger as an explicit, monitored policy rather than an ad hoc practice.
recommendations.why: RDD estimates a 8.3pp reduction in 60-day churn from RM contact at this trigger (Sharp RDD (rdrobust, robust CI)), and the no-manipulation assumption behind that estimate was directly tested (McCrary-style density check), not just assumed.
recommendations.next_step: Track RM capacity utilization against the 400-contact/month constraint used here; if capacity is regularly binding, that's the lever to negotiate for more impact, not budget.

recommendations.action: Scale the dormant/re-engagement plays (HV cashback offer, LV SMS reminder) to the full flagged population -- this is no longer a pilot-first recommendation.
recommendations.why: Both plays were tested with a genuine randomized holdout within each tier (Randomized holdout RCT (HV tier, cashback offer); Randomized holdout RCT (LV tier, SMS reminder)), not an observational comparison -- the HV cashback play alone is the single largest contributor to the optimizer's total net value protected. Randomization means treated vs. holdout is a clean causal comparison by construction; 02_validate_design.py additionally confirms the two arms were balanced on observed covariates before the offer went out.
recommendations.confidence: high -- randomized within-tier holdout, balance checked
recommendations.next_step: Keep a small (~10%) permanent randomized holdout in production even after scaling -- not to re-litigate whether the play works, but to keep a live, up-to-date effect size as take-up and the account mix drift over time.

recommendations.action: When evaluating the $100 DD-stop offer's rollout, do not judge it on early results.
recommendations.why: The effect ramps in over roughly 3 months after the offer goes live for HV accounts (event-study finding) -- evaluating impact in month 1 will understate its true effect and could kill a program that's actually working.
recommendations.next_step: Set the earliest formal evaluation checkpoint at 3+ months post-launch, not at launch+1.
